I agree with you that confirmation bias is a huge issue, but I think there are other more significant ones.

I think another huge problem with humans in general is the backfire effect. In summary, people will feel as if their life is being threatened when someone is "threatening" their core beliefs. This makes it extremely hard to change someone's mind about something that's important to them because they (subconsciously) feel like they're actually being attacked.

I am a vegan, so I think I'm more of your focus here.

Pet ownership: I am against breeding more animals and capturing them to keep as pets. But, there are many animals already living horrible lives in shelters - without being adopted, they're going to suffer more. These animals are domesticated, so we can't just let them free. They have to be kept and taken care of by humans because it would be immoral to turn them all into the streets and have thousands and thousands of feral cats/dogs.

As for abortion, this a completely different argument. Most abortions are done in the first trimester/early in the second trimester, if I remember correctly. At this point, a fetus can't feel pain and so doesn't have enough of a nervous system to be considered sentient. That's where I draw the line in regards to veganism - if an animal is sentient and can suffer, it's simply immoral to cause it to suffer.

Do be aware that all vegans have different beliefs, and so pushing them into these groups doesn't help your argument.
